ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A positive point charge A, with a charge of $Q = 2.4 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{C}$, is fixed in place. There is a point P at a distance of $l = 2 \mathrm{cm}$ from A, where the electric potential is $\varphi_p = 3000 \mathrm{V}$ (assuming the electric potential at infinity is zero). When a point charge B is moved from infinity to point P, the negative work done by the electric force is $1.8 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{J}$. If charge B is released from rest at point P, its instantaneous acceleration magnitude is $9 \times 10^9 \mathrm{m/s}^2$. The electrostatic constant is given as $k = 9.0 \times 10^9 \mathrm{Nm}^2/\mathrm{C}^2$. Only the electric force is considered.

1. Determine the maximum speed that charge B can achieve after being released.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A positive point charge A, with a charge of $Q = 2.4 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{C}$, is fixed in place. There is a point P at a distance of $l = 2 \mathrm{cm}$ from A, where the electric potential is $\varphi_p = 3000 \mathrm{V}$ (assuming the electric potential at infinity is zero). When a point charge B is moved from infinity to point P, the negative work done by the electric force is $1.8 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{J}$. If charge B is released from rest at point P, its instantaneous acceleration magnitude is $9 \times 10^9 \mathrm{m/s}^2$. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: No image evidence is needed because the problem is text-only. Following the assigned method: The negative work done by the electric force in moving B from infinity to P has magnitude 1.8×10^-3 J, so the electric potential energy of B at P is U_P = q_B φ_p = 1.8×10^-3 J. Thus q_B = (1.8×10^-3 J)/(3000 V) = 6.0×10^-7 C. The electric field at P due to A is E_P = kQ/l^2, with l = 2 cm = 0.02 m, so E_P = (9.0×10^9)(2.4×10^-6)/(0.02)^2 = 5.4×10^7 N/C. The force on B at P is F_P = q_B E_P = (6.0×10^-7)(5.4×10^7) = 32.4 N. Since the initial acceleration is 9×10^9 m/s^2, the mass of B is m_B = F_P/a = 32.4/(9×10^9) = 3.6×10^-9 kg. When B is released from rest and moves away under electric repulsion, its maximum kinetic energy equals the loss of electric potential energy: K_max = U_P = 1.8×10^-3 J. Therefore v_max = sqrt(2K_max/m_B) = sqrt((2×1.8×10^-3)/(3.6×10^-9)) = sqrt(1.0×10^6) = 1000 m/s.
